Dengue is endemic in India and prevalent during and after monsoon season. It can occur at any age but is most common in children and young adults. Symptoms (often sudden onset): - Excessive thirst (polydipsia) - Frequent urination (polyuria) - Unintended weight loss - Extreme hunger (polyphagia) - Fatigue and weakness - Blurred vision - Fruity-smelling breath (sign of diabetic

Signs: fruity breath, vomiting, abdominal pain, rapid breathing, confusion, loss of consciousness. ⚠️ EMERGENCY: Call 112 immediately if DKA is suspected. SOURCE: World Health Organization (WHO) — Influenza and Fever Guidelines CATEGORY: Fever, Influenza, Respiratory Infections TAGS: fever, headache, body pain, fatigue, chills, cough, sore throat --- FEVER --- Fever is defined as a body temperature above 38°C (100.4°F). It is a common sign of infection and the immune system's response to pathogens. Common Causes of Fever: - Viral infections: influenza, common cold, dengue, COVID-19 - Bacterial infections: typhoid, urinary tract infection, pneumonia - Other: heat exhaustion, autoimmune conditions, drug reactions Symptoms typically associated with fever: - Body temperature above 38°C - Chills and shivering - Sweating - Headache - Muscle

Symptoms typically associated with fever: - Body temperature above 38°C - Chills and shivering - Sweating - Headache - Muscle pain and body aches - Fatigue and weakness - Loss of appetite Management of Fever: - Rest and hydration (oral rehydration salts if needed) - Paracetamol (acetaminophen): 500–1000mg every 4–6 hours for adults (do not exceed 4g/day) - Ibuprofen (if no contraindications): 400mg every 8 hours - Tepid sponging for comfort - Monitor temperature every 4 hours Seek emergency care if: - Temperature exceeds 40°C (104°F) - Fever in infants under 3 months (any fever = emergency) - Fever persists

if: - Temperature exceeds 40°C (104°F) - Fever in infants under 3 months (any fever = emergency) - Fever persists beyond 3 days - Associated with stiff neck, rash, confusion, or difficulty breathing - Febrile seizure occurs --- INFLUENZA (FLU) --- Influenza is a contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses. It spreads via respiratory droplets. Symptoms of Influenza: - Sudden onset high fever (38–40°C) - Severe headache - Muscle aches and body pain - Extreme fatigue - Dry cough - Sore throat - Runny or stuffy nose - Chills Duration: 5–7 days for most symptoms; fatigue may last 2

- Sore throat - Runny or stuffy nose - Chills Duration: 5–7 days for most symptoms; fatigue may last 2 weeks. SOURCE: Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) — Gastrointestinal Disease Guidelines CATEGORY: Gastrointestinal, Diarrhea, Food Poisoning, Gastroenteritis TAGS: diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain, stomach ache, loss of appetite, bloating --- ACUTE GASTROENTERITIS --- Gastroenteritis is inflammation of the stomach and intestines, typically caused by viral (norovirus, rotavirus) or bacterial infection. Symptoms: - Nausea and vomiting - Diarrhea (watery or loose stools) - Abdominal cramps and pain - Low-grade fever - Fatigue - Loss of appetite - Headache Duration: 1–3 days (viral), up to 5–7 days (bacterial) Treatment: - Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS): Gold standard. WHO-recommended ORS composition: 2.6g NaCl, 2.9g

(viral), up to 5–7 days (bacterial) Treatment: - Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS): Gold standard. It is called the "silent killer" because it often has no symptoms until serious damage has occurred. India has a very high burden of hypertension with over 200 million affected adults. Hypertension is the single biggest risk factor for stroke. Types: - Ischaemic stroke (85%): blood clot blocking a brain artery - Haemorrhagic stroke (15%): blood vessel ruptures in the brain Recognize using FAST: - F — Face drooping: Is one side of the face drooping or numb? India has the highest TB burden in the world, accounting for approximately 26% of global cases. Pulmonary TB (lung TB) Symptoms: - Persistent cough lasting 2 weeks or more (may be productive with mucus or blood) - Coughing up blood (haemoptysis) - Chest pain - Fever (low-grade, often in the afternoons) - Night sweats - Unexplained weight

Endemic in parts of India, especially during monsoon. Symptoms: - Profuse, watery diarrhea (rice-water stools) - Rapid dehydration - Vomiting - Muscle cramps - Weakness - Rapid heart rate - Low blood pressure ⚠️ Severe dehydration can be fatal within hours — immediate treatment is essential. Treatment: - Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS): critical first step - IV fluids for severe dehydration - Antibiotics (doxycycline or azithromycin) to shorten duration

Common during and after monsoon in India, particularly in urban flooding areas. Fever resolves dramatically within 24-48 hours of treatment (diagnostic response). --- VIRAL FEVER --- A broad category of febrile illnesses caused by various viruses. Very common in India, especially during seasonal changes and monsoon. General symptoms: - Sudden onset fever (38-40°C) - Headache - Body aches and joint pain - Fatigue and weakness - Sore throat - Runny nose or nasal congestion - Redness of eyes - Rash (in some viral fevers) - Nausea (sometimes) Duration:
